# Security Incident and Breach Notification Log

Complete for every security incident, including lost devices, failed restore tests, audit-trail integrity failures, and suspected unauthorized access. Keep for 6 years. Use reference codes, not client names.

## Incident record

| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| Incident number | |
| Date and time discovered | |
| Discovered by | |
| Description | |
| Devices / files involved | |
| Was the data encrypted (FileVault on, ClinAssess locked, Time Machine encrypted)? | |
| Client reference codes possibly affected (count and list) | |
| Containment steps taken (dates) | |

## Four-factor risk assessment (45 CFR 164.402)

| Factor | Analysis |
|---|---|
| 1. Nature and extent of PHI involved (types of identifiers, sensitivity, likelihood of re-identification) | |
| 2. Unauthorized person who used or received the PHI | |
| 3. Whether the PHI was actually acquired or viewed | |
| 4. Extent to which the risk has been mitigated | |
| Encryption safe harbor applies? (PHI rendered unusable per HHS guidance) | |
| **Conclusion:** breach / not a breach (low probability of compromise) | |
| Assessed by, date | |

## Notifications (if a breach)

| Recipient | Required by | Date sent | Method | By |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Affected individuals | Without unreasonable delay, no later than 60 days after discovery | | | |
| HHS (500 or more individuals) | Within 60 days of discovery | | | |
| HHS (fewer than 500) | Within 60 days after the end of the calendar year | | | |
| Media (more than 500 residents of one state) | Within 60 days of discovery | | | |
| State agency / attorney general | Per state law: [cite] | | | |

| Corrective action | Owner | Due | Done |
